answers: Protecting people who may lack power or support
Giving everyone the same garment
Banning all use of the courts
questions.explanation: These groups are especially vulnerable, so the Torah warns against exploiting their weakness.

questions.question: What can be inferred from mentioning redemption from Egypt after these social commands?
answers: Those rescued from slavery should remember to act with justice and kindness
Only former slaves must repay debts
Egyptian courts were always just
questions.explanation: Remembering slavery and redemption teaches the Israelites not to ignore the suffering of the weak and oppressed.

questions.question: Which wording emphasizes that the command applies to Israel in the present?
answers: “Thou wast”
“Thou shalt remember”
“Out of Egypt”
questions.explanation: “Thou shalt remember” addresses the Israelites and calls them to let the past shape their present conduct.

paragraphs.title: Leaving Gifts for the Poor in the Field and Vineyard

easy.question: For whom are the grain or fruits left in the field intended?
answers: The stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
Only the owner of the field
The king and the priests
easy.explanation: The verses repeatedly say that what remains is for the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow.

easy.question: What may a person not do if he forgets a sheaf in the field?
answers: Sell it
Go back to get it
Give it to his family
easy.explanation: The verse says not to go back and fetch the forgotten sheaf, so that the needy may have it.

easy.question: What must the people remember according to verse 22?
answers: That they were wealthy in Egypt
That they were kings in Egypt
That they were slaves in Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt.”

medium.question: Why does the Torah command that part of the harvest be left for the needy?
answers: To remember slavery in Egypt and act responsibly toward others
So the field will produce less the next year
So the farmer will not need to work
medium.explanation: The reminder that Israel was enslaved in Egypt is given as a reason to care for the stranger, fatherless, and widow.

medium.question: In the phrase “thou shalt not glean it afterward,” what must the farmer not do?
answers: Work in the vineyard
Gather the grapes left behind
Plant a new vineyard
medium.explanation: The context concerns harvesting grapes, so the remaining grapes must be left for the needy.

medium.question: What order of agricultural activities is described in the verses?
answers: Gathering grapes, beating olives, and harvesting grain
Beating olives, harvesting grain, and gathering grapes
Harvesting grain, beating olives, and gathering grapes
medium.explanation: Verse 19 describes the grain harvest, verse 20 the olive harvest, and verse 21 the grape harvest.

challenge.question: What principle is shared by the grain harvest, the olive harvest, and the grape harvest?
answers: Not all the produce may be gathered; some must be left for the needy
All the produce must be given to the Temple
Only produce that falls to the ground may be gathered
challenge.explanation: In all three kinds of harvest, the people are commanded to leave some produce for the stranger, fatherless, and widow.

challenge.question: Which words emphasize that leaving produce is a command rather than merely good advice?
answers: “Thou hast forgotten”
“Therefore I command thee”
“The Lord may bless thee”
challenge.explanation: The closing words explicitly state that the Lord commands this practice.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the repeated phrase “it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow”?
answers: The command is only for poor people who live in the city
The needy must work for the field's owner
Caring for the needy is a central purpose of every kind of harvest
challenge.explanation: Repeating the same beneficiaries after each harvest emphasizes that caring for them is the lasting purpose of leaving produce behind.
